front: TC006: What is the minimum viable move?
back: Give one compliment today that names the specific thing you observed and why it mattered to you. Do not add qualifiers or requests after it.

front: TC006: What is the core sequence?
back: Specific thing -> Why it stood out -> Stop.

front: TC006: What is the field tip?
back: Name the moment, not the person.

front: TC006: What is the strong version of: Generic: 'Great job today!'?
back: The way you stayed calm when they pushed back — that changed the whole dynamic.

front: TC006: What is the strong version of: Compliment attached to a request?
back: Compliment on its own, request in a separate message.

front: TC006: What is the strong version of: Vague praise: 'You are really talented'?
back: That opening line in your talk changed the energy in the room.

front: TC006: What is better than: 'Great work — but the middle section needs redoing — but overall great!'?
back: Deliver praise and criticism in separate conversations, each allowed to land on its own.

front: TC006: What is better than: 'You are so good at this... which is why I volunteered you for the next one.'?
back: 'You are genuinely good at this.' Make the ask another day.

front: TC006: What is better than: 'You are amazing!'?
back: 'The way you re-ordered the argument made it twice as strong.'

front: TC006: What are signs it is working?
back: People light up or seem genuinely touched. The compliment does not create awkwardness. You mean it — you are not performing praise. The relationship warms without any agenda.

front: TC006: When should you avoid this technique?
back: When you are fishing for a reciprocal compliment — the motive will be sensed. In formal performance reviews where specific praise can inadvertently exclude other positive qualities.

front: TC006: What is the best recovery line?
back: 'That sounded like the set-up for bad news. It was not — there is no second half.'
